precepts.text: And the foundations of the wall of the city were garnished with all manner of precious stones. The first foundation was jasper; the second, sapphire; the third, a chalcedony; the fourth, an emerald; The fifth, sardonyx; the sixth, sardius; the seventh, chrysolite; the eighth, beryl; the ninth, a topaz; the tenth, a chrysoprasus; the eleventh, a jacinth; the twelfth, an amethyst.
precepts.point: And all thy children shall be taught of the Lord; and great shall be the peace of thy children.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

precepts.why:
Isaiah says to the afflicted, “I will lay thy stones with fair colours, and lay thy foundations with sapphires.” That is the kingdom. The Lord will lay our foundations with stones and rubies and emeralds; we are going to have a crown.

John saw that same kingdom: “And the foundations of the wall of the city were garnished with all manner of precious stones.” He names them one by one: “The first foundation was jasper; the second, sapphire; the third, a chalcedony; the fourth, an emerald; The fifth, sardonyx; the sixth, sardius; the seventh, chrysolite; the eighth, beryl; the ninth, a topaz; the tenth, a chrysoprasus; the eleventh, a jacinth; the twelfth, an amethyst.” The sapphire Isaiah promised is right there in the second foundation.

Then Isaiah goes on: “I will make thy windows of agates, and thy gates of carbuncles, and all thy borders of pleasant stones.” These are more precious stones, rubies and diamonds. The twelve tribes of Israel are the afflicted, “tossed with tempest, and not comforted”, and we have not been comforted. But the mountains shall depart, meaning destruction, while the Lord’s kindness does not depart from Israel. The city garnished with precious stones is what he is building for the people he has mercy on.

precepts.text: The holy city had twelve gates, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel. The kingdom is for God's people.
precepts.point: Video played from a 1966 CBS documentary, Black Power, White Backlash, filmed in Cicero, Illinois, where 15,000 black people worked in the factories every day but not a single black family could live: residents said they would be afraid to go out at night, that you really could not trust any of them, and one said there are many good coloreds, but the ones that are going to march I don't like. They do not like when we march, because when we march we have our pride, our dignity, and our confidence. They do not like when we stand up as the nation of Israel; it angers them and it makes them afraid.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
The holy city “had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel”.

Praises to the Most High for that. The kingdom is only for God’s people. The gates of the city carry the names of the twelve tribes, and no other nation’s name is written there.

That settles what Pam called heresy. Christ was not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel, and the city he brings has twelve gates for the twelve tribes. The same people the Lord sent into bondage with a yoke of iron upon their neck are the people whose names are on the gates.

precepts.text: Why does it say Jerusalem is builded as a city that is compact together? And had twelve gates, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel: this is our book. The kingdom is ours. The city lieth foursquare; twelve thousand furlongs: so it was 1,500 miles, the length and the breadth and the height of it equal, like a square, like a box. The wall, 144 cubits, approximately 216 feet, according to the measure of a man, that is, of the angel: so it's actually larger.
precepts.point: For there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David. Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: they shall prosper that love thee. Some of y'all busy praying for Haiti, praying for Puerto Rico, praying for Mexico, praying for America. But the Bible said pray for Jerusalem. Remember, Jerusalem's a people before it's a place. We are Jerusalem. Pray for us. We're not supposed to be praying, stop the war over there; no, we got to move them out of our land so that we can go back home.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
David says, “Jerusalem is builded as a city that is compact together: Whither the tribes go up, the tribes of the Lord, unto the testimony of Israel.” Other nations aren't there; they are not mentioned here. Why does it say the city is compact together? Revelation shows the city.

It “had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel.” This is our book. The kingdom is ours. The names on the gates are the tribes that go up.

“And the city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth: and he measured the city with the reed, twelve thousand furlongs. The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal.” So it is 1,500 miles, the length, the breadth and the height all equal, like a square, like a box. That is a city compact together.

“And he measured the wall thereof, an hundred and forty and four cubits, according to the measure of a man, that is, of the angel.” A hundred and forty-four cubits is approximately 216 feet by a man's measure, but it is the measure of the angel, so it is actually larger. That is the Jerusalem the tribes of the Lord go up to.

precepts.text: Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God. He is the God of Israel; that is the completion every feast was pointing to.
precepts.point: The feast of tabernacles, seven days unto the Lord. Tabernacle, sukkot, booth: it means to dwell.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them”. That is what tabernacle means: to dwell. He shall dwell with whom? The Israelites.

Then: “and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God.” All praises to the Most High for that. He is not the God of the Ishmaelites, not the God of the Arabs, not the God of the white man. He is the God of Israel only.

This is the completion every feast was pointing to. All seven of the high holy days read in Leviticus 23, and there are more, represent Jesus Christ, and the feast of tabernacles ends where the scriptures end: God dwelling with his people Israel for ever.

precepts.text: The nations of them which are saved shall walk in the light of it and bring their glory and honour into it; the gates are never shut; nothing that defileth enters, only they written in the Lamb's book of life. Saved means left over, Zechariah 14:16, and the nations bring their honour to the men at the gates. Only the Israelites go in.
precepts.point: The glory of Lebanon, the fir, pine, and box, shall beautify the place of my sanctuary; Lebanon and its famous trees belong to the Israelites. The sons of them that afflicted thee shall come bending, and all that despised thee shall bow at the soles of thy feet and call thee the city of the Lord, the Zion of the Holy One of Israel. That is what Revelation 3:9 said. The third temple is under Christ, not under Edom.

note.label: Prophesy From Pain to Peace

precepts.why:
“And the nations of them which are saved shall walk in the light of it: and the kings of the earth do bring their glory and honour into it.” Saved here does not mean what people get confused about. It means left over: “every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem”. Those that are left walk in the light of it: they obey the commandments, and come up to worship the King of kings and keep the feast of tabernacles.

“And the gates of it shall not be shut at all by day: for there shall be no night there.” That is the third temple, the same gates of Isaiah 60: “thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night; that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles, and that their kings may be brought.” Forces means wealth, and their kings are brought in chains. “For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish”.

“And they shall bring the glory and honour of the nations into it. And there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth, neither whatsoever worketh abomination, or maketh a lie: but they which are written in the Lamb’s book of life.” So the nations themselves are not walking in. They are bringing their glory and honour up to the men of God at the gates. Those written in the Lamb's book of life are the Israelites. Only the Israelites get in.

precepts.text: A wall with twelve gates and the names of the twelve tribes; the city lieth foursquare, twelve thousand furlongs, length, breadth, and height equal, measured by the angel; the foundations garnished with jasper, sapphire, chalcedony, emerald, sardonyx, sardius, chrysolite, beryl, topaz, chrysoprasus, jacinth, and amethyst; twelve gates of pearl and the street of pure gold.
precepts.point: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities; thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, at rest, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down, not one stake removed nor any cord broken. You will never take down Jerusalem again. Psalms 46:4-7, God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved; the heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved, he uttered his voice, the earth melted; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Psalms 48:1-2, beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, the city of the great King.

note.label: Hope Amid Destruction

precepts.why:
Psalms 122 says “Jerusalem is builded as a city that is compact together”, and Revelation 21 shows what that means: “the city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth”, measured “with the reed, twelve thousand furlongs. The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal.” It is as tall as it is wide.

Twelve thousand furlongs is about 1,500 miles by man's measurement, but it is not man's measurement: “according to the measure of a man, that is, of the angel.” It is angelic measurement, so the size is not what we are thinking.

And “the building of the wall of it was of jasper: and the city was pure gold, like unto clear glass. And the foundations of the wall of the city were garnished with all manner of precious stones.” Garnished means decorated: all kinds of fancy designs in the walls of Jerusalem. Jasper, sapphire, chalcedony, emerald, sardonyx, sardius, chrysolite, beryl, topaz, chrysoprasus, jacinth, amethyst. Each stone represented one of the tribes, the same stones the high priest wore in Exodus 28. “And the twelve gates were twelve pearls”, “and the street of the city was pure gold, as it were transparent glass.”

And the city “had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel.” So the kingdom is not for everybody. This is the Zion Isaiah 33:20 tells us to look upon, the tabernacle that shall never be taken down.

precepts.text: Sorcerers and idolaters and all liars shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone. If you are stubborn and rebellious you are dabbling in the mystic arts whether you think so or not.
precepts.point: If you cannot uphold righteousness when nobody is looking, that is your future: damnation, judgment, destruction. Stubborn goes back to bullheaded, and bullheaded goes back to Baal.

note.label: The Iranians & The Ephesians

precepts.why:
1 Samuel 15:23 said rebellion is as witchcraft and stubbornness is as idolatry. Revelation 21:8 shows where the witches and the idolaters end up.

“But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone.”

A lot of y’all think, I’m not dabbling in the mystic arts. Yes, you are. When you are stubborn and rebellious, yes, you are. It says sorcerers and idolaters. The one who in Judges 2:19 would not cease “from their stubborn way” is standing with the sorcerers and the idolaters, and their part is the lake of fire.

Psalms 78:8 makes the connection plain: “a stubborn and rebellious generation; a generation that set not their heart aright.” “The children of Ephraim, being armed, and carrying bows, turned back in the day of battle. They kept not the covenant of God, and refused to walk in his law.” That is the northern kingdom, though Judah did the same thing. Even when they got over here to the Americas they still did not keep the covenant, and that is why Assyria took the northern kingdom and why Columbus and Cortez came: because of the idolatry. The Lord was sick of it and still is, and this is the last time.

precepts.text: The city needs no sun or moon, for the Lamb is the light thereof.
precepts.point: Only those written in the Lamb's book of life enter, the twelve tribes of Israel.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
“The sun shall be no more thy light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but the Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and thy God thy glory.” That does not mean there will be no sun and no moon. They will always be there. But we are not going to need that light, because we are going to be on another level: a spiritual level, a god level.

Revelation shows the same thing: “And the city had no need of the sun, neither of the moon, to shine in it: for the glory of God did lighten it, and the Lamb is the light thereof.” That is what we just read in Isaiah 60:19.

The city is “the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.” That is what Christ meant when he said, Thy kingdom come. It “had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel.”

“Thy sun shall no more go down; neither shall thy moon withdraw itself: for the Lord shall be thine everlasting light, and the days of thy mourning shall be ended.” Everything goes back to the way it was. Israel in the kingdom lives in the light of the Lamb, and the days of our mourning are ended.

precepts.text: The kings of the earth bring their glory and honour into it.
precepts.point: Only those written in the Lamb's book of life enter, the twelve tribes of Israel.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
“And the nations of them which are saved shall walk in the light of it: and the kings of the earth do bring their glory and honour into it.” People use this to say all the nations will be saved. But saved does not mean salvation here; it is in the context of rulership. Saved from what?

The precept is Zechariah: “And it shall come to pass, that every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.” Saved means left: they were left from being destroyed. Christ did not destroy them, and they are going to obey. Walking in the light of it means they serve the King and keep the feast of tabernacles.

“and the kings of the earth do bring their glory and honour into it”, as Isaiah says: “Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night; that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles, and that their kings may be brought.”

“And there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth, neither whatsoever worketh abomination, or maketh a lie: but they which are written in the Lamb’s book of life.” Those nations do not walk in. They bring it to us at the front gate, and then they go back. Those written in the Lamb’s book of life are the twelve tribes of Israel.

precepts.text: The holy city coming down from God out of heaven.
precepts.point: Those who believe enter into rest, and those who did not believe were kept out.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.” Remember, it withdrew itself; now it is coming back.

2 Esdras 7:26 says it: “the bride shall appear, and she coming forth shall be seen, that now is withdrawn from the earth.” That bride withdrawn from the earth is the holy city Jerusalem, the access to the spirit realm, which withdrew itself from the earth. For it to be withdrawn from the earth it must once have been on the earth, and it was, during the time of Adam. Adam was not running around butt naked; Adam was going back and forth to a spiritual realm.

The city is described with twelve gates for the twelve tribes of Israel and no heathens. So the tribes were around back then, and Adam went through a gate, the Judah gate. The twelve tribes around in the beginning were called the sons of God; Moses did not name them because the Lord said to hide these things. Jacob, Esau, will never go through those gates. They may stand outside and look at it and drop some stuff off in front of it, but they will never enter into those gates.

The city was prepared from the foundation of the world; it is already built, from the beginning. It is the rest God entered, the paradise Adam was led into, and the promise of Hebrews 4:1 that we must not come short of.

precepts.text: There shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth; the unclean do not enter the kingdom.
precepts.point: The Egyptians did not practice circumcision; they were a nation of uncleanness, and the covenant was between the Lord and Israel: after the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

precepts.why:
“And there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth, neither whatsoever worketh abomination, or maketh a lie: but they which are written in the Lamb’s book of life.”

Nothing that defileth enters the kingdom; the unclean do not enter. That is why a man that comes to the truth grown must still be circumcised, even at forty, fifty or sixty years, and why the covenant nearly cost Moses his life.

precepts.text: The fearful head the list of those who take the dive into the lake of fire, before the unbelieving, the abominable, and the murderers.
precepts.point: Look at the end result of a fearful spirit that is never shaken: the fearful are the first named of those whose part is in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone. The Lord gave us the spirit of power; as long as you serve and obey him, there is nothing to be scared of.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
Look at the end result of a fearful spirit that is never shaken: “But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death.”

The fearful head the list of those who take the dive into the lake of fire, before the unbelieving, the abominable, and the murderers. That is how serious the commandment “be not afraid” is. The fearful are the first named.

precepts.text: He that is athirst is given of the fountain of the water of life freely, talking about us getting the kingdom and eternal life; he that overcometh shall inherit all things.
precepts.point: Because of his loving kindness, they shall be abundantly satisfied with the fatness of his house and drink of the river of his pleasures, for with him is the fountain of life and in his light we shall see light.

note.label: Psalm 36: The Transgression of the Wicked

precepts.why:
“For with thee is the fountain of life: in thy light shall we see light.” John sees that fountain given out: “I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end. I will give unto him that is athirst of the fountain of the water of life freely.” This is us getting the kingdom and eternal life; he that overcometh shall inherit all things.

Because of his lovingkindness, “They shall be abundantly satisfied with the fatness of thy house; and thou shalt make them drink of the river of thy pleasures.” If we keep the commandments, we are going to see that kingdom of heaven and the fatness of his house. That is why Paul says to set your affection on things above.

precepts.text: The city had twelve gates, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel.
precepts.point: This ties directly into prophecy: the gates into the inheritance carry the names of the twelve tribes only. There is no gate for the Edomite, no gate for the East Indian, because this land was given to our fathers and belongs to us. The name of the city from that day is, The Most High is there.

note.label: Ezekiel 48: The Land Divided and the Gates of the Tribes

precepts.why:
“the gates of the city shall be after the names of the tribes of Israel”: three gates northward, Reuben, Judah, Levi; three on the east, Joseph, Benjamin, Dan; three on the south, Simeon, Issachar, Zebulun; three on the west, Gad, Asher, Naphtali. John sees the same city: it “had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel: On the east three gates; on the north three gates; on the south three gates; and on the west three gates.”

This ties directly into prophecy. The gates into the inheritance carry the names of the twelve tribes only. There is no gate for the Edomite and no gate for the East Indian, because this land was given to our fathers and belongs to us.

Round about eighteen thousand measures, and the name of the city from that day is, The Lord is there. The Most High is there, and the gates are named for His people.

precepts.text: The new Jerusalem has twelve gates bearing the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel; the kingdom is for the twelve tribes, not for everyone else.
precepts.point: "Restore" means to bring back and make new. The kingdom of heaven is Jerusalem and it always belonged to Israel, not to all nations; it is not pie in the sky when you die.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
“Restore” means to bring back and make new. The kingdom of heaven is Jerusalem, and it always belonged to Israel, not to all nations. It is not pie in the sky when you die.

The new Jerusalem “had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel.” The kingdom is for the twelve tribes, not for everyone else. That is why the disciples asked, “wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?”

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

precepts.why:
“And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.” There shall be no more death. Neither sorrow. Nor crying. Neither shall there be any more pain.

Former things like what? Oppression, captivity, poverty. All that's going to be done away with. So he's going to wipe away all our tears from our eyes: that is how he binds up the brokenhearted.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 8 A Star Called Wormwood

precepts.why:
This deals with what Deacon Malachi just said about the fearful; in case you think he was talking off the top of his head, it is scripture. “Woe be to fearful hearts, and faint hands,” Woe meaning destruction be to fearful hearts and faint hands: you don't want to do the work. “and the sinner that goeth two ways!” Because you are double-minded; you go two ways, one foot in the world, one foot in Israel. Double-minded also goes into you traitors sitting amongst us learning and taking notes at last night's class while harbouring evil; your mind ain't here, it is somewhere else. The traitors that leave this truth will be on YouTube teaching what we taught them, as if the spirit came upon them and they learned it by osmosis.

“Woe unto him that is fainthearted!” The fainthearted is the fearful brother, the fearful sister. “for he believeth not;” Because you don't believe. “therefore shall he not be defended.” God says he won't defend a brother or sister like that. That is some heavy stuff right there. How would you show your belief? By your works; your works show you believe. They work together. If anything is able to move you, that means you have not believed what we preach, what God is trying to let us know: these little trials and tribulations we are going through are to purify us, just like gold, just like silver. This war is not going to be easy; God did not make it easy. You have to have faith in this, apply it, live it. Everything happens for a reason, and these scriptures are to guide us, build us up, uplift us, but a lot of times brothers and sisters don't believe; that is your unbelief.

note.label: Radicalize The Youth

precepts.why: “the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the most High”. That's the kingdom, the new heaven and new earth. “whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey him.”

note.label: Radicalize The Youth

precepts.why: “The Lord is not slack concerning his promise”. He is longsuffering, wanting repentance. “the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat”. “the earth also and the works that are therein shall be burned up.” That's how the first heaven and earth pass away: nuclear destruction. The bombs drop, everything is done away, and he makes all things new.

note.label: Radicalize The Youth

precepts.why: “Woe to the multitude of many people, which make a noise like the noise of the seas”. “and to the rushing of nations, that make a rushing like the rushing of mighty waters!” The seas are the nations, the other nations. That's precept upon precept explaining no more sea.

note.label: Radicalize The Youth

precepts.why: “These are they which came out of great tribulation”. That's us. “and have washed their robes, and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.” They serve before God's throne, and he dwells among them. “They shall hunger no more, neither thirst any more; neither shall the sun light on them, nor any heat.” No affliction. “shall lead them unto living fountains of waters: and God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes.” It's the same promise of no more tears or sorrow.

note.label: Radicalize The Youth

precepts.why: “He will swallow up death in victory”. The same thing as in First Corinthians. “and the Lord God will wipe away tears from off all faces”. “and the rebuke of his people shall he take away from off all the earth”. The Lord will remove this rebuke we're suffering. “for the Lord hath spoken it.” Young people need the end result in mind: we're going to come out on top. Endure.

moments.label: Awake and Return: Overcoming Babylon's Hypnosis

We can't play no games and be like the Pharisees and Sadducees, be covetous, be wicked, committing adultery and fornicating and lying. We want to be heard by the Lord. Jacob's trouble is at the doorstep right now, and Satan is mad because he knows he has a short time.

note.label: Awake and Return: Overcoming Babylon's Hypnosis

points: These last couple of months certain things have been going on in the congregation, and some things we never used to make known to everybody, because we know the spirit of fear could jump on some of you brothers and sisters. But we let you know about the brother they wanted to coerce into planting something in the school, and about the shooting in Jersey the other day, and because you see these things happening and see how Esau is turning up the heat on Israelites, a lot of you have become fearful. That is the spirit that jumped on you. This is for you brothers and sisters that got scared because you see the attacks coming at IUIC, at Israel. “He that overcometh shall inherit all things; and I will be his God, and he shall be my son.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 8 A Star Called Wormwood

points: “But the fearful, and unbelieving,” Understand that a fearful spirit and an unbelieving spirit go hand in hand. When you see Esau attacking the truth, the scripture says that is going to happen. You brothers and sisters in high places in this society, you have to know how to move, but don't be fearful and unbelieving: I ain't coming to the school no more, I ain't going to congregate with brothers and sisters no more, what if they take a picture of me by mistake, I'm not going to wear fringes no more, and now you don't even support the truth. That is a fearful and unbelieving spirit. You have to trust in the Most High; use wisdom and pull away from certain things, let us know, brothers, I'm in this position, try not to get pictures of me up there. We let you know the attacks and the plots coming against us not for you to become fearful and worried, but so that when it happens you are aware. If you are a police officer you have to wear a uniform on the job, you can't wear fringes there, but once you leave your job, in your leisure time you put on your fringes; that is what Esther did. Use wisdom, but if you are fearful, that is an unbelieving spirit: it is like you don't believe the Lord is going to look over you, that he is going to deliver you if anything happens to you. Everybody has a different level of faith; some brothers say I don't give a damn, they can fire me; but it is all about using wisdom. Woe be to fearful hearts, and faint hands, and the sinner that goeth two ways; woe unto him that is fainthearted, for he believeth not, therefore shall he not be defended (Ecclesiasticus 2:12-13). “and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death.”
